AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 (monster stream), copied verbatim per governing rule 3 and not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (frog_knight.py:37-42). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire. sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion -- the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering -- MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) *before* the subclass applies its powers, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: this unit's initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power that listens on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7: the four relic files and powers.py cited above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py IS hashed here for other entries); flagged explicitly as the shared finding instructs. ESCALATION CHECK: FrogKnight.cs:60-65 does TWO things -- PlatingPower at PlatingAmount and `HasBeetleCharged = false`. The amount is GetValueIfAscension(ToughEnemies, 19, 15) -> 15 = _PLATING (frog_knight.py:23). The flag reset is a no-op against a freshly constructed sim instance (a sim monster is never reused across combats; CombatState builds new ones at combat.py:134), and the sim sets the same field to False anyway. One ORDERING subtlety the shared finding does not cover, checked rather than assumed: the sim assigns _has_beetle_charged AFTER super().__init__() has already built the machine and rolled, and the HALF_HEALTH branch's lambdas read that attribute -- but the initial state is the MoveState TONGUE_LASH, so the constructor roll takes step 30's sticky early return, evaluates no condition and never touches the attribute. Executed: `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b07.py branch-order` constructs a live FrogKnight and prints its branch without raising AttributeError.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against FrogKnight.cs:67-87. Four MoveStates with matching ids (FOR_THE_QUEEN / STRIKE_DOWN_EVIL / TONGUE_LASH / BEETLE_CHARGE), one ConditionalBranchState 'HALF_HEALTH', and the same chain: FOR_THE_QUEEN -> branch, STRIKE_DOWN_EVIL -> FOR_THE_QUEEN, TONGUE_LASH -> STRIKE_DOWN_EVIL, BEETLE_CHARGE -> TONGUE_LASH (FrogKnight.cs:77-80 vs frog_knight.py:69-72). INITIAL state is TONGUE_LASH on both (FrogKnight.cs:86 passes moveState3 = TONGUE_LASH, frog_knight.py:75). No RandomBranchState anywhere, so no AddBranch integer exists to misread and the machine consumes no MonsterAi entropy at all. Intents match: BuffIntent -> BUFF; SingleAttackIntent(21) -> ATTACK 21; SingleAttackIntent(13) + DebuffIntent -> ATTACK 13 also=(DEBUFF,); SingleAttackIntent(35) -> ATTACK 35.

guards.what: HALF_HEALTH conditional: predicate, add order and the integer division (FrogKnight.cs:75-76 vs frog_knight.py:61-68)
guards.rationale: C# branch 1 is `HasBeetleCharged || Creature.CurrentHp >= Creature.MaxHp / 2` -> TONGUE_LASH; branch 2 is the exact complement -> BEETLE_CHARGE. The sim is `self._has_beetle_charged or self.hp >= self.max_hp // 2` and its complement, in the same order. Two details checked rather than assumed: (1) `MaxHp / 2` in C# is INTEGER division on two ints, so at MaxHp 191 the threshold is 95 on both sides -- the sim's `//` reproduces it, where a `/` would have given 95.5 and shifted the trigger by one HP; (2) add order is observable because ConditionalBranchState.GetNextState returns the FIRST true branch and THROWS if none match (ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54; sim state_machine.py:228-232), and executed (`monster_probes_b07.py branch-order`) the sim prints `FrogKnight.HALF_HEALTH: first-true-wins order ['TONGUE_LASH', 'BEETLE_CHARGE']`, matching FrogKnight.cs:75-76. The complements are exhaustive on both sides so the throw arm is unreachable.

guards.what: HasBeetleCharged is set INSIDE the move, before the damage (FrogKnight.cs:113-115 vs frog_knight.py:92-94)
guards.rationale: Both set the flag as the first statement of BeetleCharge, before the attack resolves. That ordering is load-bearing: the branch is re-evaluated on the roll that follows the move, and if the flag were set after a lethal-to-self attack the monster could charge twice. Both sides also make the flag one-shot for the whole combat -- nothing clears it -- so the Beetle Charge happens at most once, which is what the sim's docstring claims and, unlike PROMPT.md class 24's examples, what the code actually does.

All four match frog_knight.py:18-23 and the move bodies at :78-94, including the self-target on For The Queen and the attack-then-Frail order on Tongue Lash. `applier` is omitted on all three sim applications; see monster/stabbot's guard for the executed same-observable argument (same mechanism, same verdict).
